findings.cross_file_justification: resolve_effort (diff) returns a fourth source value "extra" that is then written to the MODELINV payload via emit_model_invoke_complete (loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py, diff) whose new effort_source parameter is documented as `caller | catalog | none`; the same three-value contract is restated at the emit site (cheval.py line 2834) and is what model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json (in the diff, truncated) is expected to encode.
findings.description: `resolve_effort` has four rungs and returns `(value, "extra")` when the resolved primary is a CLI entry carrying `extra.effort` / `extra.reasoning_effort` with no caller or catalog effort. Every other place in the diff documents `effort_source` as a closed three-value set (`caller | catalog | none`): the `emit_model_invoke_complete` parameter comment, the inline comment at the MODELINV emit call, and the resolve_effort docstring's own "caller | catalog | none" wording in FR-2. The dry-run printer already special-cases `"extra"` with a label, so the fourth value is reachable in practice (any claude-headless primary with `extra.effort` set, which is exactly the legacy config the adapter's `_resolve_effort` supports).
findings.failure_mode: When the primary resolved entry is a headless CLI entry with legacy `extra.effort` and no `--effort` / `params.default_effort`, the emitted MODELINV event carries `effort_source: "extra"`. If the payload schema enumerates the documented three values, trajectory validation of that event fails (or downstream consumers keyed on the documented set treat it as unknown), i.e. a successful invocation produces an invalid audit record.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one contract and apply it everywhere: either add `extra` to the payload schema enum and fix the two `caller | catalog | none` comments (modelinv.py param docs, cheval.py emit site), or collapse the CLI `extra` rung into `catalog` before emitting. Add a test asserting the emitted `effort_source` for an `extra.effort` CLI entry validates against the payload schema.

findings.description: `_effort` is resolved once against the PRIMARY resolved entry and then placed on `CompletionRequest.effort` for every hop in the fallback chain. The headless adapters' `_resolve_effort(request, model_config)` prefer `request.effort` over their own `extra.effort`, so a `params.default_effort` on an HTTP primary now overrides a CLI fallback hop's own configured effort, contradicting the resolve_effort docstring that calls `extra.effort` "the headless adapter's own rung". Conversely, when `_effort` is None but the answering CLI fallback resolves effort from its own `extra.effort`, `_effort_on_wire` short-circuits on `effort is None` and the MODELINV `effort_effective` reports None while the CLI was actually invoked with `--effort <x>`.
findings.failure_mode: Telemetry (`effort`, `effort_source`, `effort_effective`) describes the primary's resolution, not the hop that answered; operators debugging cost/latency on a fallback hop see a wire value that was never sent. Catalog effort on the primary silently changes the behaviour of unrelated CLI fallbacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve effort per hop (call `resolve_effort` against each hop's raw entry when building its request), or at minimum compute `effort_effective` for the final hop from that hop's own resolution rather than from the primary's `_effort`.

findings.description: `AgyOptInRequiredError` subclasses `ConfigError` (INVALID_CONFIG, retryable=False), which the cheval fallback chain treats as a hard-abort, not a walkable hop failure (see the adapter's own classification comments: ConfigError = hard-abort). Because the gate defaults to OFF, every existing deployment with `gemini-headless` anywhere in a chain now hard-aborts at that hop on upgrade unless the operator adds the new key. The "planners read it as not planned" property only holds for callers that check `agy_opt_in_enabled`/`health_check` before planning (the TS pipeline and bats-tested shell scripts); any chain that reaches the hop through cheval's own routing (e.g. `gemini-headless → gemini-api` for oversized diffs) stops walking.
findings.failure_mode: Post-upgrade, a stock Google chain whose first hop is gemini-headless returns INVALID_CONFIG for the whole invoke instead of falling through to gemini-api, on every host that has not opted in, including hosts where agy worked yesterday.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the opt-in refusal walkable (raise a ProviderUnavailableError subclass carrying `failure_class: opt_in_required`) so chains fall through to the HTTP sibling, or have the router skip gemini-headless hops when `health_check()` is False before dispatch, and call out the default flip in the migration doc.

findings.description: The gate's stated purpose is that the argv-exposed prompt is "only ever exposed by an operator's deliberate choice" and that no ambient env can flip it. But the key is read from the project config found by the cwd walk, and the agy adapter's own module docstring notes the caller's cwd is the reviewed tree. In a Bridgebuilder/Flatline run against a checked-out PR, `.loa.config.yaml` in that tree is contributor-controlled, so a PR can set `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` and opt the review host into the argv route (and into spawning `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions`).
findings.failure_mode: A contributor's PR flips the opt-in for the reviewing host; the redacted diff becomes visible to other local accounts via /proc/<pid>/cmdline for the life of the hop, defeating the FR-1 rationale. This is within the pre-existing trust model for `.loa.config.yaml`, which is why it is advisory, but the new gate claims a stronger guarantee than it provides.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the opt-in from an operator-owned location (e.g. the system defaults layer or a user-level config outside the reviewed tree) rather than the project layer, or document explicitly that the reviewed tree's config can enable it.

findings.description: `_effort_on_wire` lazily imports the private `_effort_for_model` from `anthropic_adapter` and is invoked inline inside the `emit_model_invoke_complete(...)` argument list after the model has already answered. Any exception there (ImportError/AttributeError if the private symbol is renamed, or a mapping error on an unexpected model id) propagates out of the emit expression, so a successful, paid invocation fails to write its MODELINV record and `cmd_invoke` surfaces an error after the fact.
findings.failure_mode: A refactor of the anthropic adapter's private helper, or an unexpected model id, turns a successful invoke into a crash at the audit-emit step with no MODELINV row for the spend.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute `effort_effective` before the emit call inside a try/except that logs and falls back to None, and import `_effort_for_model` at module top (or expose a public helper) so an import failure is visible at startup rather than after a billed call.

findings.description: For a `_measured` entry the test sets `cap = entry["effective_input_ceiling"]` and then asserts `entry["effective_input_ceiling"] == min(cap, ...)`, which is satisfied by any value that respects the I2 window invariant. The same pattern is applied in `test_legacy_wall_applies_only_to_anthropic_under_the_kill_switch` (`want = entry["effective_input_ceiling"]`). The calibrated branch no longer checks anything about the catalog value except the invariant already checked on the next line.
findings.failure_mode: A bad write to a calibrated entry's `effective_input_ceiling` (e.g. a typo or an un-clamped overwrite that still fits the window) passes the floor suite; the test reads as covering calibrated entries but does not.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert against the provenance instead: `effective_input_ceiling == min(ceiling_calibration.measured_input_tokens, context_window - default_max_tokens(entry))` and `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling`.
